ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus montanus* is a small gecko reaching 60 mm SVL. It features a brown dorsum with dark transverse bands and a distinct, slender, curved-toe morphology. It is endemic to Sri Lanka.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus montanus* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark, V-shaped or chevron-patterned bands across the dorsum, which are more regular than in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus montanus* inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests and rocky outcrops of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Cyrtodactylus montanus* is a nocturnal gecko that remains inactive in rock crevices during the day, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates on vertical surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus montanus* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus montanus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the high-elevation montane forests of Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
